nodes.description: Direct contact with an infectious lesion introduces Treponema carateum into the skin, where it replicates locally and produces the primary scaly papule or plaque. The inoculation site is typically an exposed extremity.

evidence.reference_title: Advances in the Diagnosis of Endemic Treponematoses: Yaws, Bejel, and Pinta
evidence.snippet: Yaws and pinta are found in warm, moist climates, mainly in forested tropical regions, and are transmitted by direct skin-to-skin contact.

nodes.description: Late lesions show epidermal atrophy and numerous melanin-laden macrophages in the dermis. Because the pigment has been relocated from the epidermis into dermal melanophages rather than merely lost, the dyschromia is structural, which is why depigmentation persists after the infection is cured and treatment restores infectivity status but not appearance.

nodes.description: The organism spreads within the skin to produce disseminated secondary lesions that remain viable and transmissible for years. Dissemination is confined to the dermis and epidermis: pinta produces none of the bone, cartilage, cardiovascular or neurological involvement seen in the other treponematoses, and this skin-limited tropism is the single feature that most distinguishes it from yaws, bejel and syphilis.

evidence.reference_title: Advances in the Diagnosis of Endemic Treponematoses: Yaws, Bejel, and Pinta
evidence.snippet: pinta is a noninvasive condition causing only local dermal lesions.

nodes.description: In early lesions the basal layer loses melanin and undergoes liquefaction degeneration, the cellular event that converts a treponemal skin infection into a pigmentary disease. This is what makes pinta unique among the treponematoses: the organism's lasting damage is to the pigmentary apparatus of the epidermis rather than to tissue architecture.

nodes.description: A single intramuscular injection of long-acting benzathine penicillin cures every stage of pinta and renders the lesions non-infectious within a day. It does not restore the pigment lost in late disease, so treatment ends transmission and halts progression without undoing the disfigurement that is the disease's lasting burden.

nodes.description: Treponema carateum maintains its peptidoglycan cell wall by penicillin-binding protein (PBP) transpeptidase cross-linking. This essential, bacteria-specific reaction is the target of the penicillin used to treat pinta: beta-lactam acylation of the PBP active site halts cross-linking and is treponemicidal, which is why a single penicillin injection cures all stages.

evidence.reference_title: From the regulation of peptidoglycan synthesis to bacterial growth and morphology.
evidence.snippet: although glycan chain polymerization occurs in the absence of transpeptidation (for example, in the presence of penicillin), efficient transpeptidation requires ongoing GTase reactions
